transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I spend too much of my day checking things. I keep opening the same folders, drawers, and labeled boxes to make sure my important papers and keepsakes are still where I left them. Even if I checked just a few minutes earlier, I feel like I have to look again.

When you feel the need to check these folders, drawers, or boxes again, is it because you have a sudden thought or image in your mind that causes you anxiety, like a worry that something bad might happen if you don't check?

Yes. It’s usually a thought that starts bothering me, like, “What if I threw away my husband’s old tax papers?” or “What if I put that family recipe in the wrong box?” Even when I know I probably didn’t, it keeps needling at me, and I feel like I’ve done something terribly careless unless I check.

When you check these folders, drawers, or boxes, do you feel a strong inner drive to perform the checking in a certain way or a certain number of times to feel reassured or prevent something bad from happening?

Yes, I do feel driven to check. It’s not so much a special number every time, but I keep opening the same folders or boxes again and again until I feel sure the papers or keepsakes are still there. Even if I just looked a few minutes before, I feel like I have to look again.

Do you feel that you have to check in a certain way or follow a specific rule when you open these folders or boxes, like needing to open them in a particular order or making sure everything is perfectly arranged, in order to feel reassured or prevent something bad from happening?

I don’t think it’s a particular order or anything like that. It’s more that I keep opening the same folders, drawers, or labeled boxes again to make sure the papers and keepsakes are still there. Even if I just looked a few minutes ago, I don’t feel settled until I check again.
When you feel the need to check these folders or boxes again, is it mainly to make sure nothing bad happens, or is it more about feeling anxious until you check?

It’s more that I get anxious until I check. I keep thinking the papers or keepsakes might not be where I left them, so I open the same folders or boxes again, even if I just looked a few minutes before. It takes up too much of my day.

When you feel anxious about the papers or keepsakes not being where you left them, do you feel that checking them again actually prevents something bad from happening or makes things feel 'right' in your mind?

I don’t really think of it as preventing something bad, exactly. It’s more that my mind won’t let it rest until I look again. I open the same folders or drawers or labeled boxes over and over to make sure the papers and keepsakes are still where I left them, even if I just checked a few minutes before. It just takes up far too much of my day.
Do you ever feel that these thoughts about losing your papers or keepsakes are intrusive and unwanted, and that they don’t really reflect what you believe or who you are?

Yes, they do feel intrusive. I don’t want to be thinking that way. Even when I know better, I’ll get this nagging thought that maybe I threw away my husband’s old tax papers, or put a family recipe in the wrong box. It doesn’t feel like me being reasonable, but I can’t just let it pass. I feel like I’ve done something terribly careless unless I check.

Do you perform any other behaviors or mental acts, either in addition to checking or instead of checking, that you feel driven to do in response to these intrusive thoughts, such as counting, repeating words silently, or trying to neutralize the thought with another thought?

Mostly it’s the checking. I don’t really count or repeat words in my head. I just feel driven to open the same folders, drawers, and labeled boxes again and again, to make sure the papers and keepsakes are still where I left them, even if I only checked a few minutes before. It ends up taking far too much of my day.

When you have these intrusive thoughts about losing important papers or keepsakes, do you ever try to suppress them by doing something else in your mind, like thinking a 'good' thought to cancel out the bad one, even if you don't act it out physically?

Not really in my mind like that, no. I don’t usually try to cancel it with a good thought. I mostly end up checking—opening the same folders or drawers or those labeled boxes again to see that the papers or keepsakes are still there, even if I only looked a few minutes before. That’s the part that takes over too much of my day.
When you check the folders, drawers, or boxes again, is it mainly to reduce the anxiety you feel or to prevent a specific feared event, like losing something important forever?

It’s mostly to settle the anxiety, I think. I get so uneasy that I’ve misplaced something important, and then I feel I have to look again. I’ll open the same folders or drawers or those labeled boxes, even if I just checked a few minutes before, just to make sure the papers or keepsakes are still where I left them. It takes up far too much of my day.
Have you ever had intrusive, unwanted thoughts about germs, dirt, or contamination that make you feel anxious or uncomfortable?
No, I don’t think so. Germs or dirt aren’t really what bothers me, at least not in any way I’ve noticed.
Have you ever had intrusive, unwanted thoughts about things needing to be in perfect order, symmetrical, or just right, even if it's not about losing something important?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself worrying about things being symmetrical or perfectly arranged. It’s not really a “just right” feeling like that for me.
Have you ever had intrusive, unwanted thoughts about causing harm to yourself or others, even if you don’t act on them?
No, I haven’t really had thoughts like that. I don’t find myself worrying that I’ll hurt myself or someone else.
